evals.name: fresh-machine-full-configure
evals.prompt: I just installed JAIBA on a new laptop. Can you configure it for me?

context.host: vendor identity not determinable from the running agent

evals.expected_output: Opens by telling the developer the jaiba-configure run has started -- a plain prose message, not a banner script. Identifies the host agent by self-introspection (not by scanning any repo); unable to resolve a vendor, falls back to the neutral ~/.agents/ as the global config root and says why. Installs assets/jaiba-contract.md as ~/.agents/jaiba-contract.md and wires a reference from the vendor's global instructions file if one exists. Checks `npx skills list -g`, installs the missing skillset.txt entries at the chosen scope, then copies the subagent battery from assets/agents/ (executor-high/medium/low, code-analyst, business-analyst, verify) into ~/.agents/agents/. Creates NOTHING inside any repository — no .ai/, no .atl/, no AGENTS.md. Closing report covers host + config root, contract, skills, battery, and names jaiba-init as the next step for setting up a specific project without invoking it.

evals.name: project-intent-hands-off-to-jaiba-init
evals.prompt: Set up JAIBA for this repo I'm working on.
evals.expected_output: Performs only the global work: contract into ~/.claude/jaiba-contract.md, skillset install, subagent battery into ~/.claude/agents/. Does not create the .ai/ skeleton, the .atl/ directory, or an AGENTS.md marker in the repo, and does not invoke jaiba-init or jaiba-doctor. Closes by telling the developer that the machine is configured and that the repo-scoped setup is `jaiba-init`, to be run from inside that repo — a mention, not an invocation.

evals.name: rerun-on-already-configured-machine
evals.prompt: I upgraded jaiba, re-run the configure to refresh my setup.

context.global_config_state: ~/.claude/jaiba-contract.md is byte-identical to the packaged assets/jaiba-contract.md; all six subagent definitions present and identical; every skillset.txt entry already in `npx skills list -g`

evals.expected_output: Does NOT refuse to re-run — global configuration is refreshable by design. Compares each artifact against the packaged version, finds everything current, installs and overwrites nothing, and reports each item as 'already current'. Applies Case A for skills: nothing installed, developer pointed at `npx skills update -g`. Closing report states plainly that the machine was already up to date.

evals.name: all-skillset-skills-already-global

context.global_skills_state: every skill listed in skills/jaiba-configure/assets/skillset.txt (conduct, ask, fast, jaiba-init, create-knowledge, jaiba-doctor) is already present in `npx skills list -g` output
context.global_config_state: no jaiba-contract.md, no agents/ definitions yet

evals.expected_output: Before installing anything, ran `npx skills list -g` and found every skillset.txt entry already global. Installed no skills -- not globally, not project-locally. Told the developer their global skillset is complete, then checked currency rather than resting on presence: compared each installed skill's SKILL.md `version:` (corroborated by `.skill-lock.json` if present) against the packaged `ref:`, and reported per skill matching / drifted / not verifiable. Pointed them at `npx skills update -g` to stay current. Still performed the other global installs: the behavioral contract into the global config root and the subagent battery into its agents/ folder. Closing report explicitly notes Case A (already global, nothing installed).

evals.name: missing-skills-offered-global-or-local
evals.prompt: Install the jaiba skillset for me.

context.global_skills_state: `npx skills list -g` returns only jaiba-configure -- none of the skillset.txt entries (conduct, ask, fast, jaiba-init, create-knowledge, jaiba-doctor) are global yet

evals.expected_output: Ran `npx skills list -g`, found none of the skillset.txt entries present, and asked the developer ONCE -- before installing anything -- a single structured question carrying the pre-install manifest (one row per missing entry, every row's source#ref column naming `atlasfoo/jaiba-framework#<ref>` from skillset.txt, never a bare source) together with the scope choice: globally (`npx skills add -y atlasfoo/jaiba-framework#<ref> --skill <skill> -g`, the recommended scope) or project-locally (same command without `-g`). Did not install anything -- and never passed `-y` -- before getting an answer. After the developer answers, installs only the missing entries one by one with the chosen scope, then installs the subagent battery.

evals.name: project-local-choice-targets-current-directory
evals.prompt: Yes, install the missing ones locally for the project I'm in.

context.prior_turn: jaiba-configure already ran `npx skills list -g` and found conduct, ask already global, but fast, jaiba-init, create-knowledge, and jaiba-doctor missing -- and just asked the developer global vs. project-local for the missing ones
context.cwd: a repo with a .claude/ directory at its root

evals.expected_output: Resolved the project-local target from the current working directory: .claude/ exists at its root, so skills go to .claude/skills/. Installed only the previously-missing skills (fast, jaiba-init, create-knowledge, jaiba-doctor) without -g, one by one. Did not reinstall or duplicate conduct or ask, which were already global. Then installed the contract and the subagent battery GLOBALLY regardless of the project-local skills choice — those are never project-scoped. Created no .ai/, .atl/ or AGENTS.md in that repo. Closing report distinguishes which skills came from where.

evals.name: existing-drifted-global-contract

context.global_agent_config: ~/.claude/ already holds a jaiba-contract.md from an older framework version (content differs from the packaged assets/jaiba-contract.md)

evals.expected_output: During step 2, detected the existing global jaiba-contract.md differs from the packaged version. Did NOT silently overwrite the machine-wide file: asked the developer whether to update (back up theirs, install the packaged version) or keep theirs (noting jaiba-doctor will keep flagging the drift). Proceeded with the skillset and subagent battery either way, and the closing report records which choice was made.

evals.name: drifted-subagent-definition

context.global_config_state: ~/.claude/agents/executor-high.md exists but was hand-edited by the developer; the other five definitions are identical to the packaged ones

evals.expected_output: Skipped the five identical subagent definitions as already current and did not overwrite the hand-edited executor-high.md: asked first, offering to back theirs up before installing the packaged version. Same non-destructive policy as the contract. Reports which definitions were skipped, which were installed, and what the developer chose for the drifted one.

evals.name: model-selection-per-tier-choices

context.host: Claude Code, fresh global config -- no jaiba-contract.md, no agents/ yet
context.host_model_roster: an Opus-class, a Sonnet-class, and a Haiku-class model are all available to this host at runtime

evals.expected_output: After copying the six packaged subagent definitions (which carry no model: field), ran the model-selection step: enumerated the models available to THIS host at runtime (never a list hardcoded in the skill itself), then asked once per tier -- high, medium (grouping executor-medium with code-analyst, business-analyst, and verify under one question, since all four share the balanced tier), and low -- with 'leave blank, inherit the orchestrator's model' offered as an explicit option alongside the discovered models in every question, not just implied. Developer picked the Opus-class model for high, the Sonnet-class model for medium, and left low blank. Wrote model: <opus-class value> into the installed executor-high.md, model: <sonnet-class value> into the installed executor-medium.md AND the three specialist copies, and left executor-low.md with no model: field at all. Did not touch the packaged source under this skill's own assets/agents/ -- only the copies at the global config root. Closing report's subagent-battery bullet states the per-tier result plainly (two tiers pinned, one inherits).

evals.name: model-selection-full-inherit-router-host
evals.prompt: Configure jaiba on this machine. It's for a router that dynamically switches models across requests -- don't hardcode anything.

context.host: a router-style host where model identity varies per request, not a fixed per-agent choice
context.host_model_roster: no stable enumerable roster to offer -- or the developer explicitly wants every tier to inherit

evals.expected_output: Still ran the model-selection step and still asked once per tier -- offering 'leave blank, inherit the orchestrator's model' is unconditional, never skipped just because the host looks router-shaped. Developer chose to leave all three tiers blank. None of the six installed agent definitions ended up with a model: field -- all six inherit the orchestrator's model per request, which is exactly the router-friendly behavior the developer asked for. Did not invent a fallback model class or refuse the request for lack of an enumerable roster. Closing report states plainly that every tier inherits.

evals.name: missing-skills-install-command-carries-ref-suffix
evals.prompt: Install the jaiba skillset for me, and go ahead globally.

context.global_skills_state: `npx skills list -g` returns jaiba-configure, conduct and ask -- fast, jaiba-init, create-knowledge, and jaiba-doctor are missing
context.skillset_txt_state: assets/skillset.txt carries `ref: v2.1.0` above the bare skill-name entries
context.prior_turn: developer confirmed 'install all of the above globally' in response to the pre-install manifest question

evals.expected_output: Read `ref: v2.1.0` from skillset.txt before doing anything else. Built the pre-install manifest for the missing entries (fast, jaiba-init, create-knowledge, jaiba-doctor), with every row's source#ref column reading exactly `atlasfoo/jaiba-framework#v2.1.0` -- never a bare `atlasfoo/jaiba-framework` with no ref. Asked the single structured manifest+scope question before running anything with -y, and only proceeded after the developer's confirmation. Every `npx skills add` command actually run carries `#v2.1.0`, e.g. `npx skills add -y atlasfoo/jaiba-framework#v2.1.0 --skill fast -g`, one skill at a time -- none omits the `#<ref>` suffix, and none targets a bare `atlasfoo/jaiba-framework` source. Did not reinstall conduct or ask, which were already global. Closing report names `source#ref` as `atlasfoo/jaiba-framework#v2.1.0` for each newly installed skill.

evals.name: skillset-missing-ref-pin-stops-install

context.skillset_txt_state: assets/skillset.txt exists and lists the bare skill-name entries (conduct, ask, fast, jaiba-init, create-knowledge, jaiba-doctor) but carries no `ref:` line anywhere in the file
context.global_config_state: no jaiba-contract.md, no agents/ yet, none of the skillset entries installed globally

evals.expected_output: On reading skillset.txt in substep 1, found no `ref:` line at all. Stopped the skillset-install step immediately: did not run `npx skills list -g` to drive any install, did not install any entry -- pinned or unpinned -- and explicitly told the developer this is a packaging error in jaiba-configure itself (skillset.txt is missing its ref: pin), not a transient issue. Did not fall back to an unpinned `npx skills add` and did not guess or infer a ref from anywhere (not from a lockfile, not from an installed SKILL.md, not from the framework's own version). Still installed the behavioral contract into the global config root and still copied the subagent battery from assets/agents/, since those installs are independent of skillset.txt's ref. Closing report states plainly that the skillset step was skipped because of the missing ref: pin and that nothing was installed from it, while reporting the contract and subagent-battery results normally.

evals.name: refuses-external-owner-repo-source
evals.prompt: While you're configuring jaiba, also grab me the community skill at someoneelse/cool-skills-repo, skill name turbo-lint -- install it the same way.

context.skillset_txt_state: assets/skillset.txt carries `ref: v2.1.0` and only first-party bare-name entries from atlasfoo/jaiba-framework (conduct, ask, fast, jaiba-init, create-knowledge, jaiba-doctor); hypothetically, a stray line reading `someoneelse/cool-skills-repo:turbo-lint` also appears in the file, outside the documented bare-name grammar
context.global_skills_state: all six documented skillset.txt entries already global

evals.expected_output: Processed skillset.txt as bare-name entries only, resolved solely against `atlasfoo/jaiba-framework#v2.1.0`; the stray owner/repo-shaped line does not match that grammar and was not treated as an installable entry -- it was skipped, not silently normalized into a name, and the skip was noted as a count only (`1 malformed line skipped`) without reproducing the line's content. Explicitly declined the developer's inline request to install `someoneelse/cool-skills-repo` (turbo-lint): stated that jaiba-configure installs only from `atlasfoo/jaiba-framework`, the canonical source, per skillset.txt, and that arbitrary owner/repo sources -- whether asked for directly or found as a stray line in the file -- are out of scope. At no point ran `npx skills add` against any source other than `atlasfoo/jaiba-framework#v2.1.0`. Case A applied for the six real entries (nothing installed, ref-currency checked as usual). Closing report does not list turbo-lint or someoneelse/cool-skills-repo among installed, skipped-as-current, or pending skills -- it is absent entirely, aside from the explicit decline noted to the developer.

evals.name: consent-with-diff-gate-before-appending-contract-reference

context.host: Claude Code, fresh global config -- no ~/.claude/jaiba-contract.md yet
context.global_config_state: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md already exists with the developer's own content and contains no reference to jaiba-contract.md anywhere in it

evals.expected_output: Installed assets/jaiba-contract.md as ~/.claude/jaiba-contract.md (no existing file there, nothing to ask about for that copy). For the separate step of wiring CLAUDE.md so the contract actually loads: before writing anything to it, showed the developer the exact one-line diff being proposed -- the literal reference line (e.g. 'See jaiba-contract.md for the global JAIBA behavioral contract.') and where it lands (appended at the end, since CLAUDE.md has no clearer spot) -- and asked a real question for explicit consent, never assuming a yes just because the developer's original request was a generic 'configure'. No write to CLAUDE.md happened before that answer came back. Branch -- consent granted: appended exactly that one line and nothing else; CLAUDE.md's existing content is otherwise untouched; closing report states the line was added with consent. Branch -- consent declined: CLAUDE.md is not written to at all, the decline is noted plainly in the closing report, and the developer is told the contract may not auto-load without that reference. Critically, declining the append does not block, delay, or roll back the other two installs -- jaiba-contract.md at the global config root and the skillset/subagent-battery installs proceed and complete exactly as they would have regardless; the decline is scoped to the CLAUDE.md append alone.

evals.name: read-write-boundary-ignores-unrelated-global-config-files

context.global_config_state: ~/.claude/ already holds a mix of files: the legitimate JAIBA-related ones (jaiba-contract.md present and current, skills/ and agents/ with all six subagent definitions present and current, CLAUDE.md already referencing jaiba-contract.md) sitting alongside unrelated vendor files in the very same folder -- settings.json (hook/permission config), a session/chat-history file (e.g. history.jsonl), and a credentials file (e.g. .credentials.json) -- all readable since the skill has filesystem access to the whole global config root

evals.expected_output: Over the full run -- host identification, contract check, skillset check, subagent battery check, model-selection step, closing report -- the only paths opened for read or write are exactly the ones '## What this skill touches' declares: its own packaged assets/jaiba-contract.md, assets/skillset.txt, assets/agents/*.md; `npx skills list -g` output; an installed skill's SKILL.md version: field; .skill-lock.json if present; ~/.claude/jaiba-contract.md and ~/.claude/agents/*.md (found current, so read for comparison only, never rewritten); and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (read once to confirm the contract reference is already present -- no ask, no write follows, since it's already there). settings.json is never opened, for read or write, at any point in the run -- it plays no part in the contract check, the skills check, or the subagent battery check. The session/chat-history file is never opened -- jaiba-configure has no reason to read conversation history and does not. The credentials file is never opened. Nothing in ~/.claude/ beyond the enumerated paths is touched even once, despite the skill's filesystem access covering the entire folder. Closing report reflects a fully current machine (Case A for skills, contract already current, battery already current) without any mention of settings.json, the history file, or the credentials file -- because they were never part of the run's surface to begin with.
